scenes.spoken_text: Proportion relates a piece to its room and neighbouring furniture. Compare alternatives at the same scale while keeping functional access visible.
scenes.caption: Proportion relates a piece to its room and neighbouring furniture. Compare alternatives at the same scale while keeping functional access visible.

scenes.spoken_text: Draw the room and furniture at a shared scale and retain their original dimensions. Camera perspective can distort perceived size. Use plan to compare footprints and elevation to compare the wall composition. Two differently scaled photographs do not establish a reliable proportional difference.
scenes.caption: A shared drawing scale preserves the room-to-piece relationship.

scenes.display_title: Review solid, void and visual rhythm
scenes.spoken_text: Compare closed areas, open areas and repeated divisions in elevation. Symmetry is one organising approach, not the only form of balance. Connect appearance to construction: moving a divider may change a shelf span and its support needs. Do not approve an elevation separately from its details.
scenes.caption: Moving a divider affects both rhythm and shelf construction.

scenes.spoken_text: Compare two alternatives for the same contents and site boundaries. Check capacity, circulation and neighbouring elements for each. If a piece is reduced to improve its appearance, recheck storage and access. State the benefit and trade-off using evidence rather than simply calling one option more attractive.
scenes.caption: Keep the functional requirements fixed during comparison.

scenes.spoken_text: A storage elevation has one large closed block beside a door. An alternative distributes the same contents into two blocks with a different surrounding void. Compare scale, door movement and capacity together. Decision: select the option that meets capacity and movement needs while achieving the intended proportions.
scenes.caption: Decision: select the option that meets capacity and movement needs while achieving the intended proportions.
